narration.full_text: Alright students, it's time for our final quiz on Control and Coordination! Let's see how well you've understood the concepts. Remember, these questions will help consolidate your knowledge. Pay close attention to each question, and try to recall the answers before they appear. Here's your first question: Write three main functions of the nervous system. Take a moment to think about it. And the answer is: The nervous system collects information from the surroundings, controls and coordinates the movement of muscles, and helps to recognise smell, taste, vision, and hearing with the help of sense organs. Next question! (a) Draw the structure of a neuron and label the cell body and axon. (b) Name the part of the neuron where information is acquired, and through which information travels as an electrical impulse. Think carefully about the parts of a neuron. For part (b): The information is acquired at the end of the dendrite tip of a nerve cell. The information travels as an electrical impulse from the dendrite to the cell body and then along the axon to its end. Moving on to the next one: 'Brain and Spinal cord are two vital organs of our body'. How is our body designed to protect them? This is an important one about protection. Here's the answer: The brain is located inside a bony box called the cranium, and a fluid, cerebrospinal fluid, acts as a shock absorber. The spinal cord is placed in the vertebral column, and the backbone protects it. Excellent! Let's tackle the next question: (i) Define receptor and state their location in our body. Mention any two receptors present in our forebrain and their functions. (ii) How do nerve impulses travel in our body? This question has two parts, so consider each carefully. For part (i): Receptors are specialised tips of some nerve cells which receive information from the surroundings, located in sense organs. In the forebrain, gustatory receptors detect taste, and olfactory receptors detect smell. For part (ii): The information acquired at the dendrite tip of a nerve cell sets off a chemical reaction that creates an electrical impulse. This impulse travels to the cell body, then along the axon to its end, releasing chemicals across the synapses. Great job everyone! You've successfully completed the quiz on Control and Coordination. Keep reviewing these concepts!

visual_beats.description: Quiz title displayed: Final Quiz: Control and Coordination
Text: "Consolidate knowledge on all aspects of control and coordination."
Question 1: Write three main functions of the nervous system.

Answer 1: (i) Collects information from the surroundings. (ii) Controls and co-ordinates the movement of muscles. (iii) Helps to recognise smell, taste, vision, hearing etc. with the help of sense organs.
Question 2 (a): Draw the structure of neuron and label cell body and axon.
Question 2 (b): Name the part of neuron: (i) Where the information is acquired. (ii) Through which information travels as an electrical impulse.
Answer 2 (b) (i): The information is acquired at the end of the dendrite tip of a nerve cell.
Answer 2 (b) (ii): The information travels as an electrical impulse from the dendrite to the cell body and then along the axon to its end.
Question 3: 'Brain and Spinal cord are two vital organs of our body'. How is our body designed to protect them?
Answer 3: Brain is located inside a bony box, named as cranium and a fluid is present in this balloon, known as cerebrospinal fluid which is a shock absorber.
Answer 3 (continued): Spinal cord is placed in a vertebral column and back bone protects it.

Question 4 (i): Define receptor and state their location in our body. Mention any two receptors present in our forebrain and their functions. Question 4 (ii): How do nerve impulses travel in our body?

Answer 4 (i): Receptors are specialised tips of some nerve cells which receive information from the surroundings. Location: Sense organs. Gustatory receptor: Detect taste. Olfactory receptor: Detect smell.
Answer 4 (ii) (part 1): The information acquired at the end of the dendritic tip of a nerve cell, sets off a chemical reaction that creates an electrical impulse, which travels to the cell body.
Answer 4 (ii) (part 2): ...then along the axon to its end, releases some chemicals, across the synapses.
